title: Generator-normalized augmented finite quotient pullback towers
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a field $k$ of characteristic $p>0$ with $p\ne\ell$, and a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $A=\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\pi$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $g:X\to Y$ be a morphism of separated finite-type $k$-schemes [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting]. On the small pro-étale sites put $C_Z=(A)_Z$, $R_Z=\mathcal O_{E,Z}$ and $S_{n,Z}=(A/\pi^n)_Z$ for $Z=X,Y$, $n\geq1$ [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf, sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients]. Write $i_Z:C_Z\to R_Z$ for the constant-function map, $r_Z=\operatorname{Res}_{i_Z}$ for scalar restriction [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars], and $g_R^*,g_C^*$ for module pullback along the canonical coefficient maps [sk-def-sfb-module-pushforward-pullback, sk-def-sfb-coefficient-morphisms].

For every cochain complex $H$ of $R_Z$-modules, there is a natural chain isomorphism
$$\beta_{Z,n,H}:r_ZH\otimes_{C_Z}S_{n,Z}\xrightarrow{\sim}r_Z(H\otimes_{R_Z}S_{n,Z}),\qquad h\otimes\bar a\longmapsto h\otimes\bar a.$$
Both sides identify with the quotient complex $H/\pi^nH$, with $h\otimes1$ mapping to the class of $h$; this specifies the inverse including balancing by nonconstant local sections of $R_Z$. All tensor products are ordinary tensor complexes [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves]. Let $P$ be any cochain complex of $R_Y$-modules, put $Q=r_YP$, and set
$$T_n=g_R^*(P\otimes_{R_Y}S_{n,Y}),\quad U_n=g_R^*P\otimes_{R_X}S_{n,X},\quad V_n=g_C^*(Q\otimes_{C_Y}S_{n,Y}).$$
Equip these with quotient transitions and augmentations $b_T:g_R^*P\to T$, $b_U:g_R^*P\to U$, $b_V:g_C^*Q\to V$. Let $d_H:r_Xg_R^*H\cong g_C^*r_YH$ be the chain isomorphism whose underlying map on $g^{-1}H$ is the identity. The balanced tensor-pullback comparison defines strict tower isomorphisms
$$\lambda:T\xrightarrow{\sim}U,\qquad\theta:r_XT\xrightarrow{\sim}V,\qquad \theta_n=g_C^*(\beta_{Y,n,P}^{-1})\,d_{P\otimes_{R_Y}S_{n,Y}}.$$
Under coefficient transport, $\lambda_n$ sends the inverse image of $h\otimes\bar a$ to the tensor of its two inverse images; $\theta_n$ sends the same inverse-image tensor to itself. The analogous constant-coefficient balancing identifies $V$ with the quotient tower of $g_C^*Q$. These formulas commute with differentials, send each transition to $h\otimes(\bar a\bmod\pi^n)$, and satisfy the strict augmentation identities
$$\lambda b_T=b_U,\qquad\theta\,r_Xb_T=b_Vd_P.$$
The statement applies to arbitrary complexes, including finite tensors that are not K-flat [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules].
